route.owner_check_file_line: THE COMPARISON of the caller with the record's owner is _scope/owner_reads.py:28-32 inside retained() (:26-34): the record's owner is loaded for (tenant, requestId) (:27, loader entry.py:232-234), then it is refused unless owner.firm_id equals the tenant (:28) AND, for any caller whose principal_class is not OPAL_GLOBAL, owner.firm_id equals the caller's firm_id and owner.principal_id equals the caller's principal_id (:29-31), AND the consumer's authorizer returns exactly True (:32; for an ordinary caller entry.py:157-159 -> requests.authorize_current, body not read; for an internal caller _scope/interactive_access.py:101-121, which returns True for OPAL_GLOBAL at :115-116 once the retained owner's firm is a concrete registered firm). It runs BEFORE the compute (:36 then :37) and again after it (:40). A SECOND check of the same kind runs inside the reader: ops/owned_requests.py _validate :171-198 -- owner.firm_id equals the data firm (:176), then authorize_current (:180), refusal REQUEST_UNAVAILABLE (:183-184) -- reached from original() at owned_report.py:338 (_materialize) and :400 (the final re-reads).
route.firm_fence_file_line: _authz/served.py:1207-1209: a caller with a selected_tenant that differs from the verified X-Firm-Id is refused FIRM_BINDING unless it is an INTERNAL subject (internal = verified_internal_subject, :1187-1191). An internal subject passes only to a registry firm (bucket_for, :1210-1214) inside its profile row's allowed list (:1224-1229; a missing list admits, a non-list or a read error refuses). Then :1232-1236: every firm restated anywhere in the event must equal the tenant, else FIRM_BINDING. Both run before the route's operation is looked up (:1239) and before any record is read.
route.order_of_checks: 1 served.py:1173-1175 contract version (CONTRACT_VERSION). 2 :1178-1180 X-Firm-Id present (else NOT_AUTHORIZED). 3 :1195-1229 the FIRM FENCE on selected_tenant (FIRM_BINDING). 4 :1232-1236 restated-firm agreement (FIRM_BINDING). 5 :1239-1241 operation known. 6 :1244 _owner_read_request (:913-942): GET only, no body, no browser owner or firm member in the query, requestId within 200 characters of letters, digits, underscore, hyphen (INVALID_INPUT). 7 :1249 -> _handle_owner_read (:944): the PRINCIPAL is resolved (:954-959): an internal subject through InteractiveAccess.current (interactive_access.py:78-99), anyone else through resolve_prospect_owner (prospect.py:22-48), which refuses unless the class is FIRM_ADVISOR or FIRM_OPERATIONS in a registered firm (prospect.py:34-35, ProspectOwnershipRefused). A CLIENT-class caller is refused HERE. 8 owner_reads.py:24 principal resolved again; entry.py:166 / owned_requests._request_id (:94-97) id shape (INVALID_REQUEST_ID -> INVALID_INPUT); 9 owner_reads.py:36 -> :27-33 THE RECORD READ and THE OWNER CHECK, in one step (the record is read at :27 and compared at :28-32); 10 compute original(): entry.py:164-166 any query member but selected_tenant is refused (UNEXPECTED_OWNED_READ_QUERY); owned_report.py:337 acceptance.get, :338 _materialize (second owner check), :356-399 the frozen composition and upload bindings, :400 final re-reads, :403 sign. 11 owner_reads.py:38 and :40 the principal and the record's owner re-read and must be unchanged. So: the fence runs FIRST and before any record is read; the record read and the owner check are ONE step (the record is read, then compared); the signer runs last.

trusted_headers.firm: X-Firm-Id (served.py:113 VERIFIED_FIRM_HEADER), read case-insensitively from the event's headers (event_headers :249-258, header :236-246). It is the TENANT. A selected_tenant query/body/path member is intent only and is compared with it (:1207).
trusted_headers.identity_set: _scope/resolve.py:104-113 TRUSTED_HEADERS, nine names: x-user-email (payload.sub, edge line 545), x-user-name (546), x-user-tier (547), x-user-role (548), x-firm-id (payload.firmId, 549), x-user-type (payload.userType, 550), x-advisor-id (551), x-advisor-role (552), x-origin-verify (constant 'cloudfront', 553). trusted_only (:203-219) drops every other header. Also X-Contract-Version (served.py check_contract_version, :1173). The render markers (resolve.py:138-142) are not used by this route.
trusted_headers.set_by: infra/aws/lambda-edge/auth-validator-edge/index.mjs:545-553 assigns each header from the verified token's payload (read: the assignments). The API Gateway authorizer naqxlm is REQUEST/CUSTOM, RS256 via Secrets Manager, attached to the route (terraform/investor-reporting/api/integrations.tf:14-20, routes.tf:52-53). The function itself verifies NO signature and no secret: it believes the headers in the event it is handed.
trusted_headers.internal_vs_client: INTERNAL: x-origin-verify == 'cloudfront' AND x-user-email present AND role not 'renderer' AND (x-firm-id == 'opal-capital' OR x-user-type == 'Dev') (served.py:313-318); the named firm-bound service subject is also admitted but is firm-bound and reaches three operations only (:289-304, :1192-1193). An internal caller becomes principal_class OPAL_GLOBAL with home_firm_id from x-firm-id (interactive_access.py:86-89). CLIENT: x-user-type 'client' (resolve.py:284) -> class CLIENT, which resolve_prospect_owner refuses (prospect.py:34). FIRM_ADVISOR: x-advisor-id present (resolve.py:293); FIRM_OPERATIONS: role or advisor-role admin with a firm (resolve.py:286). Only the last two own a request record (prospect.py:34).

how_a_caller_is_shaped: Through the portal the caller's members are set by the edge validator from a verified token, so a person is exactly the firm, type and advisor their token claims. Through a DIRECT INVOKE of irpt-status the handler is lambda_handler -> entry.handle(event) (served.py:1404-1428) with the event as handed: the invoker states routeKey, headers (every trusted member, including x-origin-verify = the constant 'cloudfront', which is not a secret), pathParameters and query. A top-level 'operation' or 'op' member even names the operation (served.py:796-799), though the owner-read gate still demands a routeKey starting 'GET ' (:918). So a direct invoker states them all: YES. The resource policy lets only API Gateway invoke (integrations.tf:66-73, AllowPortalApiInvoke-irpt-status), but any identity holding lambda:InvokeFunction on the function through its own identity policy can invoke it; that identity-side grant was not read live (not_read). Precedent: a CloudOps executor invoked irpt-status directly with constructed headers (x-origin-verify cloudfront, x-user-email, x-firm-id, x-user-role) and a constructed pathParameters/query (org/tier2_senior/0.7.0_AE_CloudOps~ANL/deliverables/y5_scripts/irptlib.py:56-63; proof IRPT_ANLREQ.TO-READS-Y5.release5-after-reads-laptop.proof_of_spec.json, scope line 64).

instruments.instrument: A direct invoke of irpt-status with a constructed event: x-origin-verify cloudfront, x-user-email a synthetic .invalid address, x-firm-id the OTHER firm, x-advisor-id a synthetic value (so the class is FIRM_ADVISOR), no x-user-type Dev, routeKey and pathParameters for the order's one request id
instruments.what_it_writes_or_logs: No table or object write: irpt-status-role is read-only (terraform/investor-reporting/ops/iam.tf:35, 'no write permission anywhere'); the signer only computes a presigned URL locally (ops/pdf_link.py:100). A refusal prints one public log line with a correlation id and records the internal one (served.py:89-108, :984-987): a CloudWatch line carrying the constructed .invalid email. The invoke itself is the only record.
instruments.who_can_use_it_today: Any identity holding lambda:InvokeFunction on irpt-status by its identity policy. The dell2 box identity cloudops-dell2-agent-user held the same grant on the SIBLING function opal-ticket-api by simulation (R6_FN1_DIRECT_INVOKE_PAIR.md section 1); its grant on irpt-status was NOT simulated here (no live call).

arms.other_firm_client: The request a seat would make (a direct invoke of irpt-status, the first instrument): routeKey 'GET /api/scoped/investor-reporting/analysis/requests/{requestId}/original', pathParameters {requestId: the id already on the order}, headers {X-Contract-Version: v1, x-origin-verify: cloudfront, x-user-email: <synthetic>@opal.invalid, x-firm-id: <firm OTHER than the record's>, x-advisor-id: <synthetic>}. TWO variants, and the code refuses them at DIFFERENT checks. (a) With queryStringParameters {selected_tenant: <the record's firm>}: refused FIRM_BINDING at served.py:1207-1209 -- the FIRM FENCE, before any record is read. This is the fence, not the owner check. (b) With no selector: the tenant is the caller's own firm, the record lives under the OTHER firm's tenant key (reports/repository.py:497-499, Key {tenant, request_revision}), so the lookup in the caller's partition finds nothing and the loader returns None (entry.py:232-234); owner_reads.py:28 refuses at its first clause -> NOT_AUTHORIZED (served.py:985). This is the owner-check STEP but its comparison clauses (:29-32) never run. NEITHER variant runs the line that compares the caller's principal with a real owner (owner_reads.py:29-31). A CLIENT-class variant (x-user-type client) is refused earlier still, at prospect.py:34-35 (NOT_AUTHORIZED), before the record is read. The comparison at :29-31 is reachable only with the record's OWN firm in x-firm-id and a DIFFERENT principal (a second person of the owner's firm), which is not 'another firm'.
arms.owner_twin: The same invoke with the record's OWN firm in x-firm-id, the owner's own principal in x-user-email, and a header set that reproduces the owner's CLASS (x-advisor-id, or an admin role with the firm; a plain role with no advisor id is refused at prospect.py:34 before the record is read), no selector. The code says: the fence is skipped (selected is None, served.py:1195, :1207), the principal resolves, the record loads (owner_reads.py:27), :28-31 hold, the authorizer must return True (:32, entry.py:157-159, body not read), the reader re-checks (owned_requests.py:176, :180), the frozen composition and upload bind (owned_report.py:356-399), then the signer returns data {download_route:{url, expires_at}, sha256, byte_length} (owned_report.py:403-406). What is recorded: the envelope's ok member, the public_reason_code if refused, and ONLY the PRESENCE (true/false) of data.download_route.url, the expires_at presence, and sha256/byte_length presence. If the original is not retained the answer is NOT_FOUND (owned_report.py:389/396). Whether the ordinary authorizer (requests.authorize_current, built by the runtime assembly) also demands the owner's advisor id and class to match is NOT READ; a refusal of the twin for that reason would be a finding, not a failure of the arm.
arms.what_is_never_written: The signed link (the url member and anything after it, including the query string); any body content of the original or of the composition; the owner's email or advisor id; a real request id beyond the one already on the order; the other firm's selected id beyond its registry name. The function writes none of these; the seat must not copy them from the response into any file, log or message either: record booleans, the reason code, the sha256 prefix at most, and the status.
arms.what_a_real_request_is_needed_for: A well-formed but nonexistent request id gets NOT_AUTHORIZED from the loader's None (owner_reads.py:28 first clause), the SAME code and text as a real record owned by another person (owner_reads.py:33). It never reaches the comparison of the caller's firm and principal with the owner (:28-31, only reachable with a loaded owner dict), never reaches the authorizer (:32), never reaches the reader's _validate (owned_requests.py:175-184) or the original's bindings and the signer (owned_report.py:338-406). A nonexistent id therefore proves only that the route does not distinguish absent from not-yours; it proves nothing about the owner check. A malformed id is refused even earlier, INVALID_INPUT at served.py:939-941 or owned_requests.py:95-96 (what the F1 census's own-firm arm got). Only a real record's owner dict puts the caller's identity against the owner.
